judge-football.justification:
Usable (8.0): The deliverables are a drill protocol (15+ graded cuts, re-stem the hitch family at about 4.7 yd/s), a "take Break G out of the price" message for scouts, and a nine-name day-3 film table with what-flips-it thresholds. The film table is openly labelled a coin flip (3 of 10 vs 4 of 10 for pick order, then 39% vs 54% on 28 receivers), and the main result is a null, so a GM gets a "don't pay for this" rather than a ranking to act on.

Football difficulty (8.8): It handles opportunity through draft-pick controls, same-year drill standardization, the drill-vs-NFL entry-speed mismatch (6.9 vs 4.7 yd/s), sample size (only 5 of 36 man/zone and slot/wide cells reach 30 snaps), selection into the NFL (116 of 149, inverse-probability weighted), and power (68% at +/-3 in). The 40-clip start offset and injuries get little or no visible treatment in the main text, and the 15-cut recommendation is not tied to a reliability number.

Unique (8.6): Asking whether the same receiver's cut in a Combine drill matches his cut on Sunday, with matched-entry-speed controls and a no-tracking benchmark, goes well beyond "does the 40 predict". The result is a null on an invented metric, which limits the upside.

Terminology (8.3): Slot/wide, man/zone, hitch/curl/comeback, SOE, NGS, and day-3 are used correctly, and real players are named (Boutte, Flournoy, Bobo, and the day-3 table). Break G is a bespoke metric whose "yd/s changed in the second around the cut" definition is awkward to read as football. Phrases like "the drill order not surviving" are also confusing, and the Figure 1 caption is dense.
top_changes: Show a drill-rep vs NFL-rep example in-text for Boutte, Flournoy and Bobo, and add a plain-language coaching read of Break G (for example, 'sheds X mph into the plant'). Cut the dense Fig 1 caption and the confusing 'drill order not surviving' phrasing. Add a one-line takeaway per named receiver: what a position coach would drill with him.

Make the day-3 section decisive. Either cut it to a short 'film list, not a ranking' note, or replace it with a receiver-level cluster-bootstrap hit rate that clears a pre-stated difference over pick order. Table 4 is wide (8 columns) and mostly empty-cell splits. Move the man/zone and slot/wide columns to the appendix and keep the what-flips-it threshold.

Give the 15-cut and hitch re-stem prescription an evidence base: a repeat-rep reliability number showing how Break G's drill reliability rises with graded cuts, plus a mention of how the 0.3 s 40-clip offset and injury or missed-season cases are handled. Trim Section 2's seven-row table to four rows (about 1,500 words total) and end on a single clear action for scouts.

judge-datascience.justification: verify.py ran and reproduced 124 of 124 numbers: 68 exact and 56 resampled with its own seeds, largest drift 10% of the interval width. My own leave-one-class-out refit of the five-covariate baseline on baseline_inputs.csv (n=116, classes 42/40/34) gave an unweighted RMSE of 15.1 against the reported 14.9, and a route-weighted RMSE of 9.7 against 8.6. The Spearman correlation of Break G with career SOE was -0.07, consistent with the null. The small gaps are probably down to fit weighting and imputation details; I did not chase them. I did not re-derive Break G from the raw frames myself. Design is sound: a no-tracking baseline of pick, 40, weight, NGS score and TE flag; leave-one-class-out validation with receiver-level bootstrap; a pre-stated +/-3 in margin with explicit power (68% at the margin, 80% only at 3.5 in); an inverse-probability weight for selection; official 3-cone and shuttle benchmarks; a noise ceiling and a measurement-error check. Models are simple, linear and shrinkage-style, which fits n~116. Break G is a new metric built from the 10 Hz signal, with an entry-speed matching test and drill-to-NFL matched receiver cards. Remaining weaknesses: the day-3 evidence rests on 28 receivers and is honestly labelled a film aid; the 54% vs 39% hit-rate comparison has an interval that touches 0; the 'weighted' RMSE of 8.6 in is described as "the size of the spread itself", which is hard to interpret; the bootstrap resamples receivers within class only; and 8 tests with a multiplicity count are mentioned only in the appendix. Table 2 also still has 7 rows.
top_changes: Replace the day-3 hit-rate comparison with a receiver-level cluster bootstrap and a leave-one-class-out test against a pre-stated margin. Report the paired difference with its n and drop the ordering claim outright if it cannot clear that margin.

Reconcile the baseline error definitions: my refit gave 9.7 weighted and 15.1 unweighted against the reported 8.6 and 14.9. Print the exact fit and weighting recipe in the appendix. Also add a baseline using shrunken (ridge or mixed-model) pick and 40 effects and a pick-only baseline, so that R2 of 0.00 is not just an artifact of OLS on five covariates.

Add a transfer-benchmark row that compares Break G with official 3-cone and shuttle against NFL Break G, with cell n. Add a Holm or FDR note in the main text for the 8 season tests. Then trim Table 2 to 4 rows by moving the robustness rows to the appendix.

judge-writeup.justification: The check passes: 1,623 words, 3 figures and 4 tables (fewer than 10 combined), with no problems flagged. The title and bold finding give the result and the football question within about 50 words, and the Break G definition sits directly under the finding. The structure follows the finalist pattern: question, metric, samples, results with named players, a team so-what, limitations and an appendix pointer. Headings carry meaning. The tone is confident and avoids overclaiming, and the power sentence is now correct. Weaknesses: the metric definition runs two sentences and is not quite repeatable by a coach, since "yards per second of velocity he changes in the second around his first cut" is clumsy and "0.22 yd/s" is unexplained. Sections 1 and 2 are still dense with nested rank-correlation rows and stacked robustness checks (random-only, top-EPA-only, matched-speed, entry speed removed) that belong in the appendix. The motivation line "clubs already price it ... 9% earlier" is stated without a direct comparison to the null result, and "2023 class's rookie deals expire" is a weak why-now. Section 4 is a nine-row, eight-column table that is hard to scan, and the sentence about 5 of 36 cells undercuts it. The bottom line is decisive, but item 3 puts statistics in a run-on sentence. Fig 1 caption contains a confusing sentence ("The drill order not surviving means...").
top_changes: Rewrite the Break G definition as one coach-repeatable sentence, e.g. 'Break G is how much speed a receiver sheds going into the plant and how hard he accelerates out, measured over the second around his first cut.' Drop 'Receivers 1 sd apart differ by 0.22 yd/s' or explain it, and tighten the garbled Fig 1 caption sentence 'The drill order not surviving means...'.

Cut Section 2 to 3 rows (Official 40 to NFL top speed, Combine to NFL Break G, matched entry speed). Move the random-only, top-EPA-only and entry-speed-removed rows plus the paragraph beginning 'Half of each receiver's sampled plays...' to the appendix. Keep one sentence on the entry-speed explanation.

Shrink the Section 4 table to Receiver, Above zero, Off-list threshold and Drill to NFL shed, and move the man/zone and slot/wide columns to the appendix. Delete 'Only 5 of 36 ... cells reach 30 sampled snaps' in favour of 'splits are too thin to read; see appendix'. In Bottom line item 3, move the 39% vs 54% comparison into a small table or a shorter sentence.

judge-viz.justification: Three main figures (the appendix has two more) and about 4 tables, so the count is well within 9. Text and figures now agree: -1.2 [-3.8, +1.0] with n=116, and rho 0.48 [0.35, 0.60] with n=92. Fig 1 is a tracking-native player card with drill and NFL traces overlaid per receiver, and it is the hero. The palette is colorblind-safe (orange and blue), and the captions state n and the takeaway. Remaining weaknesses: Fig 3B has overlapping and awkward labels (Ferguson/Mims) and the Mims leader line is odd. Fig 1 has thin traces that are faint at column width, the bottom bars mix drill and NFL without a legend of their own, and the bar panels are only a modest encoding. Fig 2 is a standard forest plot, but it is clear and shows uncertainty against a pre-stated margin. The appendix figures were not opened. The writeup text says Fig 1 is the cards and Fig 3 is the transfer scatter, so the earlier ordering request is met.
top_changes: Fig 1: shrink the bottom bars into a single dumbbell panel with a legend, and add a second row of 2 to 3 more cards, or an NFL-only slot/wide split, so the small-multiples grid shows spread, not only 3 hand-picked extremes. Thicken thin traces and use 10 pt text.

Fig 3B: fix the label collisions (Ferguson/Mims), and color or label the three Fig 1 receivers (Boutte, Flournoy, Bobo) in the scatter so the hero cards link to the population. Add a no-tracking comparison (Break G against official 3-cone/shuttle) as a faint overlay or a Panel C.

Fig 2: sort rows by group with section headers (primary, parts, no-tracking baseline), and add a baseline-R2 delta column, or an inset showing the 3 in margin as a fraction of the 8.6 in sd. Consider a day-3 queue visual (dot strip of 9 names with the film-flip condition) in place of a table.
